description: We are a two-student team interested in science, space exploration, biology, and creative problem-solving. We enjoy developing practical ideas and physical prototypes. For NASA Space Apps, we aim to combine research, design, and engineering to create an innovative and useful solution.
summary:
Our project aims to find places on Earth that have similar geological features to the Medusae Fossae Formation on Mars, especially yardangs, which are long ridges shaped by wind erosion. By studying satellite images, wind patterns, surface materials, and erosion, we want to understand the similarities and differences between these regions.
We are developing an interactive system that shows the Medusae Fossae Formation and three selected locations on Earth. Users will be able to explore these areas, compare their features, and see how similar they are through a simple scoring system. Our main goal is not just to compare Mars and Earth, but also to suggest possible research locations for future NASA missions. These places could help scientists test Mars rovers, study surface conditions, and prepare for future exploration without having to travel to Mars. Through this project, we hope to make planetary research easier to understand while offering useful ideas for future Mars exploration.
details:
What Does Our Project and How Does It Work?

Our project is an interactive digital platform designed to identify and compare geological similarities between Mars and Earth. It focuses on the Medusae Fossae Formation (MFF), a large region on Mars known for its unusual geological structures and wind-eroded landforms. 

The main purpose of our project is to help users explore Earth locations that have similar surface characteristics to this Martian region. These locations are called Mars analogs because they can help scientists better understand geological processes on Mars. Our platform brings together scientific information, geographical coordinates, geological comparisons, and 3D visualization in one place. Users can explore the selected regions and learn about their similarities and differences.

Scientific Research and Data Collection

To collect reliable information, we used NASA’s scientific resources, including:

  • NASA Mars Trek for locating and examining the Martian region.
  • HiRISE satellite images for studying detailed surface structures.
  • THEMIS data for examining surface characteristics.
  • MOLA topographic information for understanding the Martian landscape.
  • NASA Planetary Data System for additional scientific information.

Benefits

The project makes Mars analog research more accessible by combining scientific data, geological comparisons, and interactive 3D visualization within a single digital platform.

It allows users to investigate similarities between Martian and terrestrial landscapes without examining multiple scientific databases separately. The platform also highlights less commonly compared Earth regions that may provide valuable information about Martian geological processes. It supports scientific education and provides a useful starting point for future planetary research.

What Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, or Software Did We Use to Develop Your Project?

The interactive platform was developed using Framer, combining AI-assisted prompting with manual coding and website customization.

The development process involved web technologies such as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to support the platform’s structure, visual design, and interactive functionality. AI-generated suggestions and code were reviewed and adjusted during development.

The platform also integrates 3D visualizations, geographical coordinates, and scientific comparison data.

What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

The project aims to improve the understanding of Martian surface formations through comparisons with similar geological environments on Earth.

By identifying and presenting potential Mars analog regions, the platform may support future geological investigations and encourage further research into wind erosion, yardang formations, and planetary surface processes.

Its long-term objective is to develop a more comprehensive digital resource for planetary comparisons, supporting scientific research, education, and future exploration studies.

A weighted comparison framework was developed using three criteria:

  • Yardang Morphology (40%): Similarities in the shapes, orientations, and structures of wind-eroded landforms.
  • Wind Erosion (35%): Similarities in erosion processes and the effects of wind activity.
  • Surface Materials (25%): Similarities in geological deposits and their resistance to erosion.

 What Factors Did the Team Consider?

The research considered geological similarity, geographical accuracy, scientific reliability, environmental conditions, and data availability. Particular attention was given to yardang formations, wind erosion processes, surface composition, topography, and geological structures.

Differences between Mars and Earth, including temperature, atmospheric pressure, atmospheric composition, and geological history, were also considered. These factors are important because similar landforms may develop under different planetary conditions. NASA databases and published scientific studies were prioritized to support the reliability of the research. Coordinate-based calculations were used to identify and verify selected locations. When exact measurements were unavailable, approximate values were used and checked against available scientific information, while recognizing possible uncertainties.

The development process also prioritized accessibility, interactive visualization, and the clear presentation of scientific information.
